Subject: May metrics: leadership readout + QBR prep (latency / cost / uptime / usage)

Team — attaching the May dashboard and the editable workbook. High-level summary and asks below; please treat this as the source of truth for next week's leadership readout and the QBR deck.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Latency: median p95 steady but p99 spikes on 2027-05-10 during the kube runtime upgrade — impact confined to 06:15–06:45 PT; customer-facing error budget ~0.4% used.
- Cost: cost per 1M tokens up ~12% month-over-month driven by GPU spot interruptions and an increase in long-context usage for a single large customer (Acme Analytics).
- Uptime: platform SLA met at 99.92% for the month; incident on 05/10 accounted for the majority of the delta.
- Usage: overall active routes grew 14% — growth concentrated in embedding-heavy workloads.

Primary asks (action owners & deadlines):
1) Incident RCA addendum (owner: Jonas) — expanded timeline and mitigation note by Tues 5/18 COB.
2) Cost remediation plan (owner: Markus) — propose quick wins (cache TTLs, routing to cheaper model variants, tighter batching) and a 90-day plan for quantization/editioning. Initial plan by Fri 5/21.
3) QBR slide deck (owner: Laura) — use attached dashboard snapshots; add a one-pager for Acme callout (re: usage spike) and draft customer outreach language. Deck draft by Mon 5/24.
4) SLA exception pre-approval (owner: Irene) — request leadership sign-off on a temporary increased credit allowance for impacted customers; decision by Thurs 5/20.

Attachments: 2027-05-monthly-kpi-dashboard.pdf (PDF), monthly_kpi_sheet.xlsx (XLSX), qbr-prep-one-pager.docx (DOCX)

Notes and quick context:
- The p99 spike correlates with a driver rollout that affected a subset of Dedicated nodes — logs in the Drive link.
- Acme Analytics showed a 280% increase in long-context traffic (>= 4096 tokens) starting 05/04 — negotiating a dedicated capacity path (procurement looped).

Please add line-item owners in the attached workbook (column: "Action owner") and comment inline on the Acme section if you want text I can send them pre-QBR.

Thanks — K

--
Kimberly Park

Kimberly — good summary. A few thoughts from cost ops:

- Quick wins (to be delivered as an initial patch by 5/21):
  * TTL-tightening for prefix cache on embedding routes (expected 6–9% cost reduction for Acme-like workloads).
  * Route-level fallbacks: add cheaper variant (FP16-quantized) for non-LL-sensitive traffic during peak hours.
  * Dynamic batch resizing based on seq-length histogram to reduce tail token cost.

- Longer-term: a 90-day program to assess model family quantization and scheduler improvements; will include an A/B with a controlled subset of Dedicated capacity.

One blocker: we need procurement clarity for pre-allocating spot-pool buffer for critical tenants (Acme). Nimbus Cloud procurement is taking ~8–10 business days; suggest we approve a temporary credit allowance to avoid losing throughput while they finalize the contract.

I can own the cost remediation plan. Will add concrete numbers to the workbook tonight.

--
Markus
VP, Platform Economics
Redwood Inference
